analysis:
Examined the runbook change (docs/operations/model-revisions.md head 172-296) and the new scripts/models/requant.py (head 1-577).

The new flow builds weights (A-004; T-012/T-027 integrity) in CI from a template revision on models.darkbloom.ai and a pinned HF bf16 commit. It byte-compares the result with the dispatcher-supplied, locally qualified manifest_json and uploads to R2. It never promotes: promotion stays with Register Model, and providers still verify file and aggregate hashes. I found no change to provider runtime, attestation, encryption or cache code (T-041 is untouched; the new aggregate needs a new cache-routing tuple, as documented).

requant.py runs as an offline numpy tool. It uses only network GETs with range-length checks. It has no shell/eval surface, and argparse inputs are not interpolated into commands.

Hardening note, not a regression: in cmd_build, os.path.join(a.out, p) uses template manifest paths without validation. An absolute path or one containing '..' would write outside --out on the runner. The template is an already published R2 revision, and writing R2 already requires credentials, so I did not report a finding. Integration should confirm that the workflow restricts template_url to models.darkbloom.ai, as docs line 271 claims, and whether it also validates the template manifest's paths.

The docs (head 198-214) disclose these residual gaps:
- Repository R2_* secrets are readable by any workflow a writer pushes.
- keys=legacy bypasses the prod-environment secret scoping.
- The ref guard to master exists only in the workflow copy being run; the environment policy also allows v* branches and tags.
- The sole gate is one required reviewer.

These describe repository/CI configuration outside the canonical provider threat model. The workflow YAML (.github/workflows/model-requant-upload.yml) and the tests are not in this batch. Integration must verify:
- the ref guard;
- input validation before secrets are in scope;
- safe quoting of manifest_json and other inputs in shell steps (script injection);
- that only the selected key set is in scope during upload;
- conditional reservation.

The threat model has no entry for model-publication CI credentials; consider adding one.
